AdapterReport.description: The adapter a package was mapped for.

accepts.description: Config fields the adapter's descriptor says it accepts.

extensions.description:
Root extension keys the adapter's descriptor declares, for example
`nemo_fabric.plugins.v1`. The loader hands plugins, hooks and called
agents to an adapter under such a key.

instruction_mode.description: The instruction mode the loader wrote, when it wrote instructions.

BundledSkills.description:
Bundled-skill selection.

`include` and `exclude` are mutually exclusive, and neither may be combined
with `enabled: false`; a `null` list reads as omitted. An empty `include`
selects no bundled skills; an empty `exclude` selects all of them.

enabled.description: Whether bundled skills load at all.

exclude.description: Load every bundled skill except these. `None` and `[]` differ.

include.description: Load only these bundled skills. `None` and `[]` differ.

CheckerDecision.description: Whether a loaded package may start.

oneOf.description: The checker exited with 0 and its answer has `decision` set to `allow`.

The checker exited with 2 and its answer has `decision` set to `deny`,
or the checker failed.

CheckerFailure.description: Why a checker counts as failed.

oneOf.description: The program could not be started, or the report could not be written for it.
The program ran longer than the time limit. The loader ended it.

The program wrote more than 1 MiB to standard output or to standard
error. The loader ends a program that is still running. The result
is the same when the program had already ended by itself: it has no
exit code and no answer.
The program ended with an exit code that is neither 0 nor 2, or a signal ended it.

The program wrote something that is not one JSON object, or a
`decision` that does not fit its exit code. For a checker URL: the
answer is not HTTP, or not a JSON object with `decision` set to
`allow` or `deny`.

The checker URL could not be reached: no address, a refused
connection, or a connection that broke.
The checker URL answered with an HTTP status other than 200.

CheckerResult.description:
What the checker answered about one loaded package, and what the load made of it.

The checker is a program the caller names in the options. It is asked once,
after the package passed its own checks and was mapped, and before anything
starts.

answer.description:
The JSON object the checker wrote. The load reads its `decision` and
nothing else. The order of its keys is not kept, and a number is kept
as a JSON number, so a long whole number can lose digits. None: the
checker wrote no single JSON object, or it was not started, ran past
the time limit or wrote more than it may. What such a checker wrote
is not read.

decision.description: Whether the package may start. A checker that failed is a `deny`.

detail.description:
More about a failure, as text: why the checker could not be started,
that it wrote more than it may, or else the end of what it wrote to
standard error. None: the checker did not fail, or there is nothing
to add.

exit_code.description:
The exit code of the checker. None: it was not started, it ran past
the time limit, it wrote more than it may, or a signal ended it.

failure.description: Why the checker counts as failed. None: it answered as it must.

env.description:
Environment variables visible to the harness and its tools.

Values are serialized into the run plan and can appear wherever configs
or plans are logged or persisted. Prefer `api_key_env`-style
environment-variable-name indirection for credentials.

env_names.description:
Names of environment variables visible to the harness and its tools,
with values read from the NeMo Fabric process environment.

Only the names are serialized into the run plan. NeMo Fabric reads each
value when it starts or invokes the adapter and fails if one is unset.
Values must remain unchanged while a runtime or service is active;
restart the runtime and any associated service to use changed values.

ModelReport.description:
What was configured for the model. The model each run used is not reported here.

The caller's `models.default` is the model choice. A config that sets none
offers a model by naming a `models` entry with the text of the document's
default model, and the loader moves that entry to `models.default`. A
config that holds one model under another name has chosen that model. The
loader writes no model of its own.

ResponseLimits.description:
Inclusive budgets for a buffered invocation result and declared artifact files.
Omitted fields retain the default budget. These limits are owned by the SDK,
independently of the harness and execution environment.

Keep the adapter's native state in a folder named after the agent, so
every runtime of the agent uses the same folder. Requires an artifact

SkillConfig.description:
Skill capability configuration.

A non-null `directories` requires an empty `paths`, and a non-null
`duplicates` requires a non-null `directories`; `null` reads as omitted.

bundled.description: Bundled-skill selection. `None` preserves the harness default.

directories.description:
Structured external-skill entries, resolved relative to the config base
directory. Each entry names one skill folder (`skill`) or a folder of
skills (`folder`). Supply only when `paths` is empty; an empty list loads
no external skills. `None` means not set.

duplicates.description:
Policy for two `directories` entries that provide skills with the same
name. Requires `directories`. `None` preserves native handling.

paths.description: Skill paths resolved relative to the config base directory.

SkillDirectory.description:
One structured external-skill entry: exactly one of `{"skill": path}` or
`{"folder": path}`. The other key may be present only as `null`, which
reads as absent.

oneOf.description: One skill's folder; it must contain `SKILL.md`.
A folder of skills discovered by the selected adapter.

SkillDuplicatePolicy.description: How two `skills.directories` entries that provide the same skill name resolve.

oneOf.description: Start fails, naming both entries.
The later entry's skill loads.
The earlier entry's skill loads.
